# Building a Data Lab: provenance, splits and deletion on 10,299 human activity windows

A behavior model needs more than a large dataset. Researchers must know where observations originated, which uses are permitted, how evaluation units remain independent, and which data can be retained. We implemented a bounded offline intake-to-export workflow on a public human activity dataset.

![Study overview](/assets/research/ac08-cover.svg)

## Provenance and intake

The [W3C PROV Data Model](https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-dm/) describes entities, activities and agents and their relationships. Our small receipt uses these concepts to trace an input, transformation and output; it is not a full PROV-conformant implementation.

We obtained [UCI Human Activity Recognition Using Smartphones](https://doi.org/10.24432/C54S4K), Anguita et al. (2013), licensed CC BY 4.0, from its official distributor. A public license does not imply consent for every new research purpose or for reidentification. Our scope is aggregate quality assessment without individual tracking.

The archive has 61,005,872 bytes and SHA-256 c00b803081a5c797cd5e4b83700a9810b38d53d9d84e01917e090e1fdbc81031. We recorded UTC retrieval time and hashes for the official train/test subject, label and feature files. Downloads had a size cap; selected archive members were read in memory.

## Schema and split validation

| Split | Windows | Participants | Features |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| train | 7,352 | 21 | 561 |
| test | 2,947 | 9 | 561 |

We checked all 5,777,739 feature values across 10,299 windows for finiteness, validated row counts and label/subject ranges, and confirmed zero subject-ID overlap. This does not establish absence of every kind of leakage, window dependence, representativeness or reidentification risk.

![Observed activity counts](/assets/research/ac08-distribution.svg)

## Minimal export and reproducibility

The export contains exactly twelve aggregate rows and three fields: split, activity and windows. No participant IDs or individual features are included. Python Counter and an independent SQLite aggregation agree. Reacquiring the source and running optimized Python reproduced the CSV byte for byte and all receipt fields except retrieval time. Six tests passed in normal and optimized Python. Each run removed its downloaded archive in a finally block and checked the path was absent.

![Intake to deletion](/assets/research/ac08-lineage.svg)

Unlinking a downloaded file does not prove deletion from filesystem snapshots, backups, upstream sources, existing caches or trained weights.

## Next evidence

Keep Manager training and ManagerBench evaluation separate, and maintain provenance and purpose restrictions. This study is an offline public-data aggregate pipeline, not new participant consent, production ingestion, revocation or model-unlearning verification. Production adoption needs independently reviewed rights, authorization, retention, deletion propagation, access controls and availability-time checks. Follow-up [issue #863](https://github.com/Daisuke134/anicca-ops/issues/863). No Manager weights or production app changed.
